stories.headline: Putin hails Russia’s test launch of ‘most powerful missile in the world’ Russian leader says the nuclear-capable Sarmat missile will enter combat service at the end of the year.
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the successful test launch of the Sarmat missile, dubbed "Satan II" by NATO, which he claims is the most powerful missile in the world. The nuclear-capable missile has a warhead yield more than four times greater than any Western equivalent. Putin stated that the Sarmat missile will enter combat service at the end of the year, replacing the aging Soviet-built Voyevoda. The test launch was conducted on Tuesday, with Putin hailing it as a significant achievement. The Sarmat missile is expected to bolster Russia's nuclear capabilities, with Putin emphasizing its superior power compared to Western counterparts. The missile's entry into combat service is slated for later this year, marking a significant upgrade to Russia's military arsenal.

stories.headline: UAE condemns hijacking of oil tanker carrying Egyptian sailors off Yemen The UAE has condemned the hijacking of an oil tanker while sailing off the Yemeni coast, carrying a number of Egyptian sailors, and the subsequent diversion of
stories.summary: The UAE has condemned the hijacking of an oil tanker carrying Egyptian sailors off the Yemeni coast. The vessel was subsequently diverted into Somali territorial waters, posing a threat to maritime security and international trade routes. The UAE foreign ministry warned of the dangers of the incident, affirming full solidarity with Egypt and supporting efforts to secure the release of the Egyptian sailors. The Arab Parliament Speaker, Mohammed bin Ahmed Al Yamahi, also denounced the hijacking, calling for intensified global anti-piracy measures. The UAE emphasized the need to protect maritime security and ensure the safety of international trade routes, and is working to resolve the situation and ensure the safe return of the sailors. The incident has raised concerns about piracy in the region and the need for increased cooperation to prevent such incidents.

stories.headline: Dela Rosa: Former Philippine ‘drug war’ police chief runs away from government agents to avoid ICC arrest warrant Scurrying through the backhalls and stairwells of the Philippine Senate, trailed by aides and falling over at least once, the large, bald man was trying to evad
stories.summary: Senator Ronald dela Rosa, a former Philippine national police chief, has taken refuge in the Philippine Senate to avoid arrest. He is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) for his role in former President Rodrigo Duterte's "drug war". Dela Rosa, also known as "Bato", was seen rushing through the Senate's backhalls and stairwells, trailed by aides, in an attempt to evade local agents. The chaotic scene unfolded as he sought to avoid an ICC arrest warrant. Dela Rosa spent the night at a Senate office after another Duterte ally offered him refuge. His actions come as the ICC investigates alleged human rights abuses during Duterte's presidency, in which Dela Rosa played a key role as police chief. The incident has sparked chaos in the Philippines.

stories.headline: US denies mediating Somalia political dispute as election tensions grow Mogadishu (HOL) — The United States has denied reports that it is directly mediating talks between Somalia’s federal government and opposition leaders as politi
stories.summary: The United States has denied reports of directly mediating talks between Somalia's federal government and opposition leaders amid growing election tensions. The denial comes after claims that Washington was hosting talks at the heavily fortified Halane compound to resolve a dispute over the country's electoral process. Somalia is facing a political crisis as President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term nears its end, with fears of instability in Mogadishu. The US Embassy in Somalia had been reported to be preparing to host talks between the federal government and opposition leaders. However, the US has clarified that it is not directly mediating the talks, despite previous reports of pressure on both parties to enter negotiations to ease the growing crisis. The situation remains tense as Somalia edges closer to a potential crisis.

stories.headline: Google Unveils Googlebook, A New Laptop Category Built For Gemini Intelligence
stories.summary: Google has unveiled Googlebook, a new laptop category built around Gemini intelligence. The Googlebook series will run on a foundation combining Android and ChromeOS, offering seamless device integration. Key features include the Magic Pointer, which uses Gemini to provide contextual suggestions. The laptops will be manufactured in partnership with Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo. A distinctive design element, called the glowbar, will be featured on each device. This announcement comes over 15 years after Google introduced Chromebook. The Googlebook series aims to provide a new level of intelligence and functionality, leveraging Gemini's capabilities to enhance the user experience. The devices are expected to offer a unique blend of Android and ChromeOS, setting a new standard for laptops. Google's partnerships with major manufacturers will help bring Googlebooks to a wide range of consumers.

stories.headline: Chinese scientists create self-destructing ‘living plastic’ that can break down in six days
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have created a self-destructing "living plastic" that can break down in six days. The material is degraded by two strains of the common bacterium Bacillus subtilis, which work together to produce different polymer-degrading enzymes. When placed in a nutrient broth at 122 degrees Fahrenheit, the spores activate and the film fully degrades within six days. The process does not create microplastic particles, making it a potential solution for reducing plastic waste. The researchers engineered the two strains of Bacillus subtilis to improve the efficiency of destruction. The study was published in the journal ACS Applied Polymer Materials, demonstrating the effectiveness of this new approach to breaking down plastic materials. The self-destructing plastic requires the right disposal route to fully degrade, but it shows promise for reducing plastic waste.

stories.headline: Microsoft starts expiring critical Secure Boot certificates in just 2 weeks
stories.summary: Microsoft is expiring critical Secure Boot certificates in two weeks. The certificates, set to expire on June 24, 2026, are crucial for ensuring the security of the boot process on Windows devices. If not updated, devices will still function but may be vulnerable to security risks. Microsoft recommends prioritizing the update to maintain protection. The expiration is part of Microsoft's support cycle, which includes ending support for Windows 10 in October 2025. Extended Security Updates (ESU) are available for Windows 10, version 22H2, for those who cannot upgrade to Windows 11. Microsoft provides tools and guidance to help users proactively update their Secure Boot certificates, ensuring devices remain secure and protected against potential vulnerabilities that may be discovered after the expiration date. Updates are necessary to prevent exposure to security risks.

stories.headline: ESA Expands XR Tools For Space Exploration
stories.summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is expanding its use of Extended Reality (XR) tools for space exploration. XR technology, which includes virtual and augmented reality, is being utilized to open new pathways for space exploration. The ESA is leveraging XR to enhance its space missions, providing new ways to train astronauts, design spacecraft, and conduct spacewalks. The agency's XR tools also enable scientists to better visualize and analyze data from space, leading to new discoveries and insights. The expansion of XR tools is part of the ESA's efforts to stay at the forefront of space technology and exploration. With a staff of around 3,000 people globally, the ESA is committed to advancing its space exploration capabilities through innovative technologies like XR. This development is expected to play a significant role in future space missions and discoveries.

stories.headline: Anthony Edwards Admits Timberwolves Have No Answer For Victor Wembanyama
stories.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves suffered a brutal 126-97 loss in Game 5 against the San Antonio Spurs. Anthony Edwards acknowledged that the team has no answer for Spurs center Victor Wembanyama, who dominated the game with 27 points, 17 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 blocks on 56.25% shooting. Edwards admitted that some of Wembanyama's moves were unstoppable, stating "Tonight, some of the stuff that Wemby was doing, you don’t really have too much of an answer for it." Wembanyama's impressive performance led to the significant loss, highlighting the challenge the Timberwolves face in containing the talented Spurs player. The loss puts the Timberwolves in a difficult position, and they will need to regroup to counter Wembanyama's impact in future games.

stories.headline: Ayesha Zafar's rapid ton crushes Zimbabwe
stories.summary: Ayesha Zafar's unbeaten century propelled Pakistan to a 153-run victory over Zimbabwe in the first T20I at the National Bank Stadium. Zafar's rapid ton, 102 runs, was a key factor in Pakistan's win. The team's innings started strongly despite Muneeba Ali's early dismissal for two runs. Captain Fatima Sana also contributed with an all-round performance. Pakistan's win sets the tone for the three-match series. The match was part of Zimbabwe Women's tour of Pakistan in 2026. Ayesha Zafar's century was a record-breaking feat, showcasing her batting prowess. The significant margin of victory highlights Pakistan's dominance in the match. The series will continue with the remaining two T20I matches.

stories.headline: Canadiens' bad start, lack of opportunism costly in Game 4 loss to Sabres
stories.summary: The Montreal Canadiens failed to capitalize on opportunities in their 3-2 Game 4 loss to the Buffalo Sabres, evening the series. Despite having seven power plays, the Canadiens scored on only one, courtesy of Cole Caufield. Goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made crucial saves to thwart the Canadiens' other chances. The team mismanaged the puck, squandering six power play opportunities. A win would have given Montreal control of the series, but instead, the Sabres tied it up with Zach Benson scoring the winner. The Canadiens' lackluster start and inability to seize chances proved costly, as they failed to generate sufficient shot volume on power plays, emblematic of their overall performance. The loss marks the third time in the Stanley Cup playoffs that the Canadiens have failed to capitalize on a golden opportunity.

stories.headline: Southampton to play Hull at Wembley for Premier League place
stories.summary: Southampton will play Hull City for a place in the Premier League after beating Middlesbrough 2-1 in extra time of their Championship playoff semi-final second leg. The match was closely contested, with Southampton coming back from a goal down to secure the win. Hull City had previously booked their place at Wembley with an impressive win. The Championship playoff final between Southampton and Hull City is scheduled to take place on Saturday, May 23, 2026, at Wembley Stadium in London. The winner of this match will earn a spot in the Premier League. Southampton's victory over Middlesbrough sets up a thrilling showdown with Hull City, with the stakes high for both teams. The match promises to be an intense and closely watched encounter.

stories.headline: After NEET-UG 2026 Cancellation, Plea In Supreme Court To Replace NTA & Conduct Fresh Exam Under Judicial Supervision
stories.summary: The Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA) has filed a petition in the Supreme Court alleging "systematic failure" by the National Testing Agency (NTA) in conducting the NEET-UG 2026 exam. The plea, filed through advocate Tanvi Dubey, seeks the replacement of NTA with a "more robust, technologically advanced, and autonomous body" to conduct NEET examinations. FAIMA has urged the Court to direct the Union Government to re-conduct NEET-UG 2026 under the strict supervision of a judicially appointed, high-powered committee chaired by a retired Supreme Court judge. The petition also requests the Court to order either the replacement or major restructuring of NTA. The plea aims to ensure a fair and transparent examination process for NEET-UG 2026 candidates. A decision on the petition is awaited from the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Prateek Yadav News LIVE: ‘Extremely saddening,’ says Akhilesh Yadav on step-brother's death
stories.summary: Prateek Yadav, the 38-year-old son of late Samajwadi Party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav, has passed away in Lucknow. He was the half-brother of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. Prateek Yadav died after a prolonged illness and was rushed to a hospital in Lucknow, where he was declared dead by doctors. The exact cause of his death has not been revealed yet. Akhilesh Yadav expressed deep sorrow over his step-brother's death, remembering him as a hardworking and health-conscious individual. In a statement, Akhilesh Yadav said Prateek Yadav's demise is "extremely saddening" and offered humble tributes. BJP leader Aparna Yadav arrived at her home in Lucknow following the news of Prateek Yadav's death. The family is yet to release an official statement on the cause of his death.

stories.headline: Training aircraft crashes near Baramati airport in Maharashtra, probe under way
stories.summary: A training aircraft operated by Red Bird Aviation crashed near Baramati airport in Maharashtra's Pune district on Wednesday. The two-seater plane was on a routine training session when it developed a technical glitch while flying at low altitude, prompting an emergency landing. The incident occurred in an open field near Gojubavi village adjacent to the airport. The aircraft suffered damage but details on injuries or casualties are not available. This incident comes months after another crash involving a flight carrying Ajit Pawar. An investigation into the cause of the crash is currently underway. Police are gathering information and examining the circumstances surrounding the incident. The crash highlights concerns over aviation safety and the need for thorough investigations to determine the cause of such incidents. A probe is ongoing to determine the exact cause of the technical glitch.

stories.headline: AIMIM leader’s house, where Nashik TCS case accused Nida Khan had stayed, demolished
stories.summary: A house belonging to AIMIM corporator Mateen Patel in Kausar Baug, Nashik, was demolished by civic officials and police personnel. The property was allegedly built illegally and had been served notices. Patel had come under scrutiny after Nida Khan, an accused in the Nashik TCS sexual harassment and religion conversion case, was found to have stayed at his house. The demolition was carried out amid a row over the property's illegal status. Nearly 100 officials took part in the pre-dawn demolition. The action was taken by the municipal corporation, with the property being on the list of buildings facing bulldozer action due to alleged illegal construction. Patel's party has backed him, while other politicians have raised concerns over the issue, with some linking it to urban terrorism and jihad.

stories.headline: “Europe Moves Its Borders Outside Europe: Return Hubs Plan Sparks Political Earthquake” EU ministers consider offshore asylum processing centres in Africa and beyond, in a controversial shift reshaping migration geopolitics.
stories.summary: EU ministers are considering a controversial shift in migration policy, exploring the creation of offshore asylum processing centers in Africa and beyond. This move would allow the European Union to process asylum claims outside of its borders, potentially reshaping migration geopolitics. The plan, known as "return hubs," aims to improve the management of migration flows and reduce the number of asylum seekers arriving in Europe. The proposal has sparked debate, with some member states expressing concerns about the feasibility and ethics of such a plan. The EU is seeking to establish partnerships with countries in Africa and other regions to host these processing centers, which would enable the union to screen and process asylum claims before allowing successful applicants to enter Europe. This policy shift could have significant implications for global migration patterns.

stories.headline: Inflation and Geopolitics Roil Markets as Investors Eye Fed's Next Move The S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined amid rising inflation concerns and U.S.-Iran tensions.
stories.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined due to rising inflation concerns and escalating U.S.-Iran tensions. As quarterly earnings season comes to a close, investors are shifting focus to the Federal Reserve's next move. Tech shares dropped, negatively impacting the Nasdaq, while the Dow remained positive thanks to gains in the healthcare sector. Market tensions are rising amid inflation and global events, with the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq experiencing significant declines. Investors are awaiting fresh inflation data, Fed speeches, and additional earnings reports. Any progress toward de-escalation in the Middle East could lead to a relief rally, while renewed disruptions may push the market back toward recent lows. The upcoming week will be closely watched for cues on the market's direction, with inflation and geopolitical events being key factors.

stories.headline: Markets React to Rising Inflation and Tumultuous Geopolitical Climate The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq slipped from record highs amidst higher-than-anticipated inflation data and an uneasy U.S.-Iran ceasefire.
stories.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped from record highs due to higher-than-anticipated inflation data and an uneasy US-Iran ceasefire. The Dow ended higher, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq slid as chip stocks dipped from records. Inflation reached a 3-year high, and Treasury yields rose as oil prices gained. However, overnight markets showed major US benchmarks finishing near their best levels after reports of a potential US-Iran memorandum to end the war. Previously, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq notched record highs, boosted by gains in AI-related stocks such as Nvidia and a stronger-than-expected jobs report. The recent market performance is impacted by concerns over valuations and geopolitics, with investors closely watching the developments in the US-Iran situation and their effects on the economy. The market volatility is expected to continue amidst these uncertainties.

stories.headline: Wall Street Highlights: S&P 500, Nasdaq Sink on Hottest Inflation Reading in Years, Jump in Oil Technology stocks were the biggest laggards after weeks of outsized gains, with heightened risks around geopolitics and inflation adding another level of uncertainty
stories.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices declined due to the highest inflation reading in years and a surge in oil prices. Technology stocks, which had experienced significant gains in recent weeks, were the biggest losers as concerns over geopolitics and inflation added to market uncertainty. The core Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose more than expected in April, driven by higher energy costs and supply disruptions related to the conflict in the region. As a result, US equity futures and bonds fell, with the Nasdaq 100 plunging over 2% in its steepest single-day sell-off in weeks. The S&P 500 also dropped, retreating from its all-time highs, as investors reacted to the inflation report and rising oil prices. The market decline was fueled by concerns over elevated valuations and the potential impact of inflation on the economy.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today Live: Stock to buy today: Sagility Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 13 May
stories.summary: Indian stock markets reopened on May 11, 2026, after a brief closure. The BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 are being closely monitored for live updates and share price movements. Investors can track top gainers and losers, as well as IPO details and corporate announcements on platforms like Angel One and NSEindia.com. The NIFTY 50 share price chart is available on Groww Terminal, providing historical data and technical indicators. Share Market Today provides live updates, latest share prices, and mutual fund information. The BSE Sensex heat map is a useful tool to track stock performance, including gainers, losers, and volume toppers. Investors can access real-time data and analysis to make informed decisions about their investments in the Indian stock market. Live updates and news are available on various financial websites and platforms.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Snap Four Days of Losses; End Marginally Higher The 30-share BSE Sensex rose 49.74 points, or 0.07 per cent, to settle at 74,608.98. During the day, the index touched a high of 75,191.57 and a low of 74,134.4
stories.summary: The 30-share BSE Sensex rose 49.74 points, or 0.07 per cent, to settle at 74,608.98, ending a four-day losing streak. The index touched a high of 75,191.57 and a low of 74,134.48 during the day, fluctuating 1,057.09 points. Indian stock markets closed marginally higher despite geopolitical uncertainties and fluctuating crude oil prices. Metal stocks surged after the government increased import duties, while IT stocks declined. The rupee hit a fresh lifetime low, but midcap and smallcap indices recorded gains. The Sensex had opened 0.5% lower at 74,171, marking its fifth consecutive session of losses, due to volatile markets, elevated crude oil prices, and sustained foreign outflows amid the Iran conflict. However, it managed to recover and end the day in the green, snapping its four-day losing streak.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Dalal Street Finally Sees Green! Sensex Jumps, Nifty Crosses 23,450 as Metal Stocks Shine Stock Market Today: After Two Days of Bloodbath, Dalal Street Finally Finds a Pulse Again, Sensex rebounds over 200 points as traders breathe easier after panic
stories.summary: The Indian stock market rebounded after two days of decline, with the Sensex jumping over 200 points and the Nifty crossing 23,450. Metal stocks led the gains, with the Nifty Metal index surging 2.56%. Other sectors, including oil and gas, pharma, and infrastructure, also traded in the green. This recovery comes after a significant decline on previous days, where the Sensex had trimmed over 1,000 points and the Nifty50 had dipped below 23,900. The market had been affected by inflation woes and a Budget-day hangover, but Monday's session saw a spirited comeback, with the Sensex increasing by 944 points to reach 81,666, a 1.17% rise. The rebound has brought relief to traders, with the market finally seeing a positive trend after a period of decline.

stories.headline: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex rises 300 pts, Nifty below 23,500; SMIDs gain, metal, bank stocks lead Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates Wednesday: At pre-open, the Nifty50 and the Sensex declined, tracking mixed global cues
stories.summary: The Indian stock market saw a rise in the Sensex by 300 points, while the Nifty remained below 23,500. Mid-cap and small-cap stocks gained, with metal and bank stocks leading the Sensex. Initially, the Nifty50 and Sensex declined at pre-open, tracking mixed global cues. However, the market later pared early gains and traded lower. On the previous day, the Indian equity markets ended higher, with the NSE Nifty jumping 0.83% to close at 23,777.80. The broader markets outperformed frontline indices as investors showed renewed interest in midcap and technology stocks. The stock exchanges will reopen on May 11, 2026.

stories.headline: Nigeria recorded an estimated $446.6 million loss in oil revenue in April despite a modest increase in production to 1.66 million barrels
stories.summary: Nigeria experienced a significant loss in oil revenue, estimated at $446.6 million, in April. Despite a modest increase in oil production to 1.66 million barrels per day, the country's output remained below federal expectations. The loss is attributed to a global oil surplus, with production expected to exceed demand by 0.8 million barrels per day in 2025 and 0.6 million barrels per day in 2026. This surplus is partly due to increased production in other countries, such as the US, which recently returned to record oil production rates, supplying 13.6 million barrels per day to the market. The global oil market trends are expected to continue affecting Nigeria's oil revenue in the coming years.

stories.headline: Accelerating organic revenue growth of +5.3% TDA yoy...
stories.summary: A company reported accelerating organic revenue growth of +5.3% year-over-year, with strong market share gains of +365 basis points for the group and +210 basis points for Adecco. The Health, Wealth & Career segment achieved 4% organic growth, despite a 5% revenue decline to $1.26 billion due to the TRANZACT divestiture. Free cash flow increased to $838 million in the first nine months of 2025, up from $724 million in the same period last year. U.S. revenue saw a 6% organic decline, but improved to 2% growth in the second half. Adjusted operating profit declined 13% to £222 million, with a reported adjusted operating margin of 28%, in line with company expectations. Aon's Reinsurance Solutions division delivered 8% organic revenue growth to $379 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.

stories.headline: Bitcoin rolled back to $81,200 after dipping to $79,800 on Tuesday's hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation reading, while BNB zoomed 2.5% over 24 hours and dogeco
stories.summary: Bitcoin rebounded to $81,200 after dropping to $79,800 following a hotter-than-expected US inflation reading on Tuesday. The cryptocurrency had initially dipped in response to the inflation news but managed to recover. Meanwhile, BNB saw a 2.5% increase over 24 hours, and dogecoin added 1.3%. This growth occurred as crypto funds experienced their strongest weekly inflows in months. The US inflation reading had sparked initial volatility in the crypto market, but Bitcoin was able to regain its footing above $81,000. The gains in BNB and dogecoin outpaced other major cryptocurrencies, with BNB leading the way with its 2.5% increase. Overall, the crypto market saw a mix of volatility and growth in response to the US inflation news.

stories.headline: New UK business risk report reveals shift in priorities Marsh Risk’s UK Business Risk Report helps organisations prioritise actions, allocate capital and engage with insurers more effectively.
stories.summary: Marsh Risk's UK Business Risk Report surveyed over 2,000 UK business leaders, providing comprehensive insights into key risks facing businesses. The report identifies a shift in priorities, with cybercrime, market competition, and service disruptions being major concerns. Business leaders are now viewing interconnected risks as the "new normal," with a constantly evolving web of risks. The report aims to help organisations prioritise actions, allocate capital, and engage with insurers more effectively. It offers industry-level insight and practical recommendations, covering businesses from sole traders to those with over 250 employees. The findings highlight the complexity of risks faced by UK businesses, with the report serving as a guide for organisations to navigate these challenges and make informed decisions. The survey provides a snapshot of the current risk landscape, informing business strategies and insurance engagement.

stories.headline: DeepMind spinout Isomorphic Labs raises $2.1 Billion to design drugs with AI Isomorphic Labs secures $2.1 billion to advance AI-designed drug development, partnering with major pharmaceutical companies for innovative treatments.
stories.summary: Isomorphic Labs, a DeepMind spinout, has raised $2.1 billion in a Series B funding round led by Thrive Capital. The funding round also received backing from Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG, and the UK Sovereign AI Fund. The company aims to use the funds to advance its AI-designed drug development and expand its pipeline, bringing candidates closer to clinical testing. Isomorphic Labs is partnering with major pharmaceutical companies to develop innovative treatments using artificial intelligence. The $2.1 billion investment will help the company scale its AI drug design engine and accelerate its mission to make AI-designed drugs a reality. This significant funding round marks a major milestone for Isomorphic Labs as it works to revolutionize the field of drug discovery with AI technology.

stories.headline: Elon Musk 'wanted 90%' of OpenAI, CEO Sam Altman says during feisty tech titan trial Elon Musk was obsessed with trying to control OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company's CEO Sam Altman said
stories.summary: Elon Musk was obsessed with controlling OpenAI, the company's CEO Sam Altman testified in a trial. Altman stated that Musk wanted 90% of OpenAI, indicating a strong desire for control. The trial, which pits tech titans against each other, saw Altman spar with Musk's lawyers. Altman recalled a moment when Musk suggested that control of OpenAI should pass to his children if he were to die, describing it as "hair-raising." Musk's lawyer accused Altman of prioritizing profit over people. The testimony highlights the intense interest Musk has in the artificial intelligence company, with Altman's statements shedding light on the billionaire's intentions and behavior regarding OpenAI. The trial continues, with the tech world watching the developments closely.

stories.headline: Here’s What Musk And Altman Have Said About Each Other At Trial Musk’s lawsuit accusing Altman and OpenAI of abandoning their mission as a non-profit has shed light on their workings at the artificial intelligence giant.
stories.summary: Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI has begun trial, shedding light on the workings of the artificial intelligence giant. Musk sued OpenAI, Altman, and president Greg Brockman in 2024, alleging they abandoned their non-profit mission. Musk co-founded OpenAI with Altman a decade ago, with the goal of developing artificial intelligence as a non-profit. However, Musk claims Altman steered the company away from its original mission. The trial has presented two different accounts of OpenAI's evolution, with Musk arguing that Altman's actions were a betrayal of the company's founding principles. The lawsuit is being heard in Oakland, marking a significant legal battle between two prominent tech figures. The case centers on whether OpenAI's transition from a non-profit to a for-profit entity was a breach of its original mission.

stories.headline: Grok downloads fall nearly 60% Elon Musk’s xAI chatbot is struggling to compete with similar artificial intelligence projects from OpenAI, Meta and Google, per the Wall Street Journal.
stories.summary: Elon Musk's xAI chatbot, Grok, is experiencing a significant decline in user engagement and market position. Downloads have fallen nearly 60% since January, from over 20 million to 8.3 million by April, according to AppMagic. Paid user adoption remains low at 0.174%, compared to ChatGPT's 6%. Grok, once positioned as a challenger to industry leaders, is struggling to compete with similar AI projects from OpenAI, Meta, and Google. The chatbot's user base and revenue growth have stalled, with enterprise adoption also underperforming. This downturn indicates a loss of momentum for Grok in the competitive AI market, where other chatbots have gained more traction and user engagement. The decline in downloads and paid adoption raises concerns about Grok's long-term viability and competitiveness.
